answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, externally costly bond before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. A contract records the bond and slashes it when a seeded audit proves fraud, while honest agents recover it after a delay. This makes a velvet swarm of disposable accounts expensive: the attacker must tie up capital per identity and risks losing it, rather than gaining influence by minting names. The atlas of accounts may grow, but the garden stays costly to poison.
